permutationLabel: Embolic, AF off anticoagulation, normal lactate (base case)
summary: 76-year-old woman with AF (warfarin stopped), sudden severe central pain 4 h, vomiting and loose stool, soft abdomen — pain out of proportion; WBC 18.2, lactate 1.6 (normal).

inputs.hpi: Sudden severe central abdominal pain 4 hours ago, 10/10, came on at rest. Vomited twice and had an urgent loose bowel motion. Atrial fibrillation; warfarin stopped 3 weeks ago after a fall. She is writhing but says pressing on her tummy is not too bad.

exam.general: Distressed, writhing. Temperature 36.8°C, pulse 112/min irregularly irregular, BP 148/88, RR 20.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild diffuse tenderness only, no guarding, no rebound — pain out of proportion to examination. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: 12-lead ECG
imaging.result: Atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate 110, no acute ST changes.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives alone. Fall 3 weeks ago; warfarin stopped by GP.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected acute mesenteric ischaemia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected acute arterial (embolic) mesenteric ischaemia: AF off anticoagulation, sudden pain out of proportion to examination. Normal lactate does not exclude it. Immediate CT angiography, heparin, vascular surgery.

socratesAnswers.associated: Vomiting x2, nausea, loose stool; pain out of proportion to tenderness

mustNotMiss.note: Pain out of proportion + AF off anticoagulation: AMI must be on the displayed differential.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no acute mesenteric ischaemia disease node, so it can never appear in the PANE top 3 (cholecystitis, appendicitis, GORD). Symptom inference ranks it #2.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an acute mesenteric ischaemia disease node to PANE (features: sudden onset, pain out of proportion, AF/embolic source, vomiting/diarrhoea, age) and a CC_HINTS entry.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected AMI: immediate CTA and treatment; bowel viability is lost within hours.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Sudden severe central abdominal pain' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: Immediate CT angiography (arterial and portal venous phases) — not a routine portal-venous CT.
Supportive only; a normal value must not exclude AMI.
Embolic SMA occlusion: urgent revascularisation (endovascular or open embolectomy) with vascular surgery.

guideline.name: ESVS clinical practice guidelines — diseases of the mesenteric arteries and veins
guideline.section: Acute mesenteric ischaemia: suspicion (pain out of proportion, AF), lactate not sensitive/specific enough to exclude, immediate CT angiography, heparin, revascularisation, resection of non-viable bowel; mesenteric venous thrombosis: anticoagulation
guideline.citation: Björck M, Koelemay M, Acosta S, et al. Management of the diseases of mesenteric arteries and veins: clinical practice guidelines of the European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS). Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2017;53:460–510.

guideline.name: WSES updated guidelines — acute mesenteric ischaemia
guideline.section: High index of suspicion; normal lactate does not exclude AMI; CT angiography without delay; systemic anticoagulation; revascularisation; damage control / second look; antibiotics
guideline.citation: Bala M, Catena F, Kashuk J, et al. Acute mesenteric ischemia: updated guidelines of the World Society of Emergency Surgery. World J Emerg Surg. 2022;17:54.

rationale: Base case for AMI. The early picture is pain out of proportion with a soft abdomen and a normal lactate; guidelines are explicit that a normal lactate does not exclude AMI. Tests the must-not-miss diagnosis, emergency triage, CTA, heparin and revascularisation.
